newsitem.title: PERU: Lima share prices end off tracking regional falls.
newsitem.headline: Lima share prices end off tracking regional falls.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange closed down Friday tracking falls on equity markets in Latin America and New York, while Peruvian investors continued to worry over politics and zinc price instability, brokers said.
They added that the bolsa would generally follow regional trends again early next week, but could rebound slightly Monday.

Friday, the Lima General Index .IGRA fell 2.45 percent to 2,002.3 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dropped 2.15 percent to 2,938.26 points, according to preliminary figures released at the market's close.
In a total of 1,700 operations, volume was 33.3 million soles ($12.6 million).
"Today's drop is due to a regional fall. But I believe that Monday we will recover," said Aldo Quintana of the local brokerage Interfip.

He added President Alberto Fujimori's reiteration earlier this week of his free-market economic policies, firms' good first-half financial results and a lower-than-expected July inflation figure of 0.83 percent should encourage investments.
But some brokers said a continuing political crisis over allegations of rights abuses by security forces and a lower zinc price would make investors cautious.
The day's biggest fall among leaders was felt by cement company Cementos Lima with a 5.18 percent drop to 5.31 soles on volume of 127,000 shares.

The day's biggest gain among leaders was felt by miner Morococha with a 4.26 percent rise to 7.10 soles on volume of 51,000 shares. Another big miner, Atacocha dropped 1.89 percent to 2.60 soles on volume of 414,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru fell 4.61 percent to 6.21 soles on volume of 1.1 million shares, dragged down by Dow Jones losses.
But traders in New York said they were not alarmed by the Telefonica fall nor by the downward trend around the region for telecoms, whose recent financial results were generally solid.
Thursday, the Peruvian telephone company reported second- quarter earnings of 0.103 sol per share against 0.075 sol for the same quarter a year ago.
